## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9fd5fcc3d525a96c5a966b87f4bc26f65f71f31c`

Reviewed from git only: `refs/review/pr-10619` (head `9fd5fcc`) diffed against merge-base `adeecd666868d11aa0fc132f42298306f1e88742`; `refs/review/main` at `c2d86599b334dc97fa225bca2e0fa57df9044739`. Three files in the diff: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-ref-check.ts` (+55/-2), `flow-ref-check.test.ts` (+43/-0), `.changeset/10538-cel-macro-bound-variable.md` (+7). Evidence: the card and its three comments, the triage ruling `5830908145`, the claim `5831034609`, the PR body, the check-runs at the head, and my own run of the head and merge-base sources (extracted from git into the review scratch dir, i18n import stubbed, run with node strip-types) over the PR's 13 pin expectations plus 34 adversarial sources. `/home/user/objectui/node_modules` is absent after the container restart, so the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` and `@objectstack/formula@17.4.0` were read, read-only, from the pnpm virtual store under `/home/user/objectui-issue-10545/node_modules/.pnpm/`. The os-dev-report comment was not used as evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

Binding text. Triage `5830908145`: 「treat the iteration variable of `map` / `filter` / `exists` / `all` / `exists_one` as bound inside its macro; pin the canonical example ⇒ `[]` and a genuinely unknown root ⇒ flagged.」 Claim `5831034609` scope: 「the iteration variable is bound inside its macro's body only; the same name outside the macro is still a root」; pins: 「the canonical example reports nothing; `rows.map(r, r.subject) + r` still flags the trailing `r`; an unknown root is still flagged with its suggestion」; file surface: 「`flow-ref-check.ts` (`rootIdentifiers` / `findUnknownRefs` only), pins beside its existing tests, and one `.changeset/10538-…md`」.

Behaviour changes, each at the head:

1. `flow-ref-check.ts:82` — `COMPREHENSION_MACROS` is the set `map`, `filter`, `exists`, `all`, `exists_one`. Exactly the five the triage rules on, nothing more. RIGHT.
2. `flow-ref-check.ts:100-120` — new module-private `macroBindings(src)`. Regex at line 103 matches a member call whose name is followed by a bare identifier and a comma; line 106 keeps only the five macros; line 107 takes the call's open paren; lines 108-116 walk to the depth-matched close paren, or the source length while unclosed; line 117 records `{ name, open, close }`. Bound span is that macro's own argument list. RIGHT against 「bound inside its macro's body only」.
3. `flow-ref-check.ts:128` — bindings are computed on `noStrings`, the same string-stripped text the root scan reads, so indices agree and a paren inside a string literal cannot close a span. Verified: `rows.map(r, r.subject == "a)") + rows` ⇒ `[]` at head. RIGHT.
4. `flow-ref-check.ts:136-142` — the root scan records each identifier's index and skips it only when a binding of the same name has the identifier strictly after its open paren and strictly before its close paren. The declaration position is inside; the receiver (before the paren) and anything after the close are outside. Verified at head: `r.map(r, r.x)` flags `r`; `rows.map(r, r.x) + r + rows.map(r, r.y)` flags `r`; `rows.exists(r, r.ok) && r.items.all(i, i.ok)` flags `r`; `rows.map(r, rr.x)` flags `rr` not `r`. RIGHT against 「the same name outside the macro is still a root」.
5. `flow-ref-check.ts:138` — `m.index` renamed to `at`; same test, same slice. No behaviour change. RIGHT.
6. `flow-ref-check.ts:16-18` — header bullet documenting the rule. True to lines 82-142. RIGHT.
7. `flow-ref-check.ts:152-183` — `findUnknownRefs` body is byte-identical to the merge-base: the template-hole scan, de-dupe, `RUNTIME_GLOBALS`, `$`-prefix skip and suggestion search are untouched. Verified: a template hole `Hi {rows.map(r, r.name)} {r}` still flags the trailing `r`; empty scope still returns `[]`. RIGHT.
8. The canonical example is real: `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` `dist/automation/index.d.ts`, the `AssignmentValue` JSDoc, reads 「`joinNonEmpty(rows.map(r, r.subject), "\n")` builds a digest body from a list」. Merge-base source reports `r` on it; head reports `[]`. RIGHT.

Adversarial sources at head, all as CEL semantics require: whitespace before the paren, multi-line arguments, nested parens in the body, chained macros (`rows.filter(x, x.done).map(y, y.id)`), an outer variable read inside an inner macro, same-name shadowing, sibling macros, a parenthesised or deep receiver, a `$`-prefixed receiver, a bound name equal to a known root, an underscore variable — all `[]`. A non-macro name (`mapx`), a capitalised `Map`, a global-style `map(r, r.x)`, a non-identifier first argument (`r.x` or a string) bind nothing and still flag. An unclosed macro binds to the end of the source, the conservative direction the file header declares. `cel.bind(x, rows, x.size())` still flags `cel` and `x` before and after; it is outside the ruled five and the PR says so.

Asked and missing: nothing. Five macros bound (test `flow-ref-check.test.ts:82-89`, one expectation per macro plus the three-argument `map`); canonical example pinned to `[]` (`:77-80`); a genuinely unknown root still flagged, with its suggestion (`:107-109`, `rowz` ⇒ `rows`) and without (`:111-113`); the claim's own `rows.map(r, r.subject) + r` leg (`:95-97`).

Done and not asked: the header bullet at `:16-18` and the private helper, interface and constant at `:78-91`. All in the one file the claim names and serving `rootIdentifiers` only; no other file is touched. The second commit `9fd5fcc` is a merge of `origin/main` `adeecd6` with no content of its own. Not a breach.

Existing pins edited or deleted: none. The test file is additions only (`+43/-0`); the source's two removed lines are the replaced one-line doc comment and the `m.index` rename.

New pins can fail. Lit control, my run of the merge-base source against the eight new `it` blocks: canonical, five-macros, nested, inner-outside, receiver and `rowz` fail (six), matching the PR body's 「Tests 6 failed | 15 passed (21)」; after-close (`:95-97`) and `join` (`:111-113`) pass on base, which the PR body states and which is their job, guarding against over-binding. Negative legs present: `:95-113`, five of them, each expecting a non-empty result.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/10538-cel-macro-bound-variable.md:1-3`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. Two `src/` files of a `fixed`-group package changed (`.changeset/config.json` lists `@object-ui/app-shell` in `fixed`), so AGENTS.md line 168 and `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` require a declaration, and one is present. AGENTS.md 版本号策略: no `major` in a changeset; a behaviour fix to an advisory warning with no new or changed export is a `patch`. Level is RIGHT. Not a `content/docs`-only change, so the empty-frontmatter rule does not apply. Check-runs `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check` and `Changeset Overwrite Report` all success at the head.

Changeset prose, sentence by sentence:
- Title 「the flow designer's "not in scope" warning no longer flags a CEL comprehension macro's own iteration variable」 — TRUE (item 4 above; canonical `[]` at head).
- 「`findUnknownRefs` read every root identifier in a CEL source as a flow variable, so the `r` in `rows.map(r, r.subject)` drew an amber "not in scope" warning.」 — TRUE. Merge-base reports `r`; the callers render it amber with `role="note"` (`FlowEdgeInspector.tsx:258-261`, `FlowExprIssue.tsx:39-43`) or as `level: 'warning'` (`flow-expr-problems.ts:50-51`).
- 「That included the assignment-value example in `@objectstack/spec`, `joinNonEmpty(rows.map(r, r.subject), "\n")`.」 — TRUE (item 8).
- 「The scanner now treats the first argument of `map`, `filter`, `exists`, `all` and `exists_one` as a variable bound inside that macro's own argument list.」 — TRUE (`:82`, `:103-117`, `:142`).
- 「The same name used outside that list (after the closing parenthesis, or as another macro's receiver) is still checked as a root, and an unknown receiver is still flagged with its suggestion.」 — TRUE (`test.ts:95-109`; my probes).
- 「The warning stays advisory; nothing about what blocks Save changes.」 — TRUE. No caller changed; `validateExpressionClient` (the `role="alert"` error path) is untouched; the diff touches no save path.

Docs and README prose added by the diff: none besides the in-file JSDoc. `:78-80` 「Each is receiver-style … and its first argument DECLARES the iteration variable instead of reading one」 — TRUE for CEL. `:89` 「or the source length while it is still unclosed」 — TRUE (`:108`). `:97-98` 「`src` must already have its string literals stripped」 — TRUE, the one call site is `:128` on `noStrings`. `:140-141` 「(the declaration included)」 — TRUE, the skip uses strictly-after-open.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR body's own flags. (a) 「Why the local scanner and not the parser-backed reader (H2, measured)」: reproduced on the installed `@objectstack/formula@17.4.0`; `collectCelRootIdentifiers` returns `["rows","r"]`, `["rows","x"]`, `["rows","e"]`, `["rows","a"]`, `["rows","o"]` and `["rows","r","i"]` for the six table rows, exactly as the body states, so switching to it would keep the defect; the choice to fix the local scanner is sound and objectstack is not edited, consistent with the claim's file surface. (b) `cel.bind`: the scanner half (flags `cel` and `x` before and after) is verified; the upstream `evaluate` value of `3` I did not reproduce, my probe did not bind variables the way that API expects. It is outside the ruled five and not load-bearing. (c) 「no page under `content/docs` describes this designer warning」: TRUE; the one `not in scope` hit, `content/docs/guide/react-pages.md:290`, is about a React page `ReferenceError`, a different surface. `packages/app-shell/README.md` does not mention the warning. No open questions are listed in the body.
- CI at head `9fd5fcc`, polled 12:19Z, 12:23Z and 12:25Z: final count 43 check-runs, 40 success, 3 skipped (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)`), 0 failure, 0 in progress. All eight `Test (shard n/8)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Line Citation Gate`, `README Export Check`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Build & E2E` are success. The PR body's local vitest and gate counts were not re-run here (no node_modules in the review checkout); the shards are the evidence.
- Draft: YES. The PR is a draft at review time; it needs un-drafting before merge. Not a contract defect.
- `Clause-②: no` HOLDS. `findUnknownRefs`, `scopeRoots`, `describeUnknownRefs` and `UnknownRef` keep their signatures; the additions at `:82-120` are module-private; `flow-ref-check.ts` is not re-exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` and the package `exports` map is unchanged. The warning is advisory in all four callers, so no accept set moves.
- Main under the PR's files: did NOT move. Three commits landed on `main` after merge-base `adeecd6`; none touches the three PR files. `mergeable: true`, state `behind`.
- AGENTS.md #11 (cite by content): the diff carries no path-line citations; the test name and comments cite `objectui#10538` and the `AssignmentValue` symbol. Line Citation Gate success.
